title: Manage security through the information-system lifecycle: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Which lifecycle activity must create or validate this security decision or evidence artifact?
focalInsight: Traceability from stakeholder need through operation and disposal keeps security accountable across change.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Information System Lifecycle
nodes.definition: Coordinated stages from stakeholder need through retirement with traceable security decisions.
nodes.detail: Coordinated stages from stakeholder need through retirement with traceable security decisions.
nodes.decision: Place each requirement, design, control, evidence, owner, exception, and risk decision in its proper stage.
nodes.failureExample: A security requirement appears only after deployment, with no design trace.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Lifecycle security connects decisions and evidence across change.

nodes.label: Stakeholder Requirements
nodes.definition: Mission, business, safety, privacy, legal, operational, and risk needs expressed by accountable parties.
nodes.detail: Mission, business, safety, privacy, legal, operational, and risk needs expressed by accountable parties.
nodes.decision: Elicit before design so conflicts and acceptance conditions can be resolved.
nodes.failureExample: An architect assumes availability expectations without consulting operations.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Stakeholders define the required outcome and constraints.

nodes.label: Requirements Analysis
nodes.definition: Refinement of needs into testable, traceable, nonconflicting requirements.
nodes.detail: Refinement of needs into testable, traceable, nonconflicting requirements.
nodes.decision: Use when turning broad goals into properties, threats, measures, owners, and acceptance criteria.
nodes.failureExample: “Protect customer data” has no classification, threat, or test condition.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Analysis makes a security requirement actionable.

nodes.label: Architecture Design
nodes.definition: Choice of trust boundaries, controls, interfaces, dependencies, and residual-risk treatment.
nodes.detail: Choice of trust boundaries, controls, interfaces, dependencies, and residual-risk treatment.
nodes.decision: Decide before implementation and revisit after material change.
nodes.failureExample: A service is built before its identity and data-flow boundaries are specified.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Architecture turns requirements into enforceable structure.

nodes.label: Implementation
nodes.definition: Construction and configuration of the designed system under controlled change.
nodes.detail: Construction and configuration of the designed system under controlled change.
nodes.decision: Use approved code, libraries, baselines, reviews, and configuration evidence.
nodes.failureExample: A developer bypasses a design control to meet a release date.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Implementation must preserve the approved security design.

nodes.label: Integration
nodes.definition: Connection of components, identities, interfaces, data flows, and dependencies into an operating system.
nodes.detail: Connection of components, identities, interfaces, data flows, and dependencies into an operating system.
nodes.decision: Test the boundaries and failure behavior introduced when parts are combined.
nodes.failureExample: Two secure components exchange an unauthenticated message at their interface.

nodes.label: Verification Validation
nodes.definition: Evidence activities that check conformance to requirements and suitability for intended use.
nodes.detail: Evidence activities that check conformance to requirements and suitability for intended use.
nodes.decision: Verify stated requirements and validate the system’s effective use and outcome.
nodes.failureExample: A system passes a unit test but fails the business recovery requirement.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Verification asks whether it was built to spec; validation asks whether it meets intended need.

nodes.label: Deployment
nodes.definition: Authorized transition into operation with approved configuration, readiness, rollback, and acceptance.
nodes.detail: Authorized transition into operation with approved configuration, readiness, rollback, and acceptance.
nodes.decision: Require operations ownership, monitoring, access, backup, incident, and recovery readiness.
nodes.failureExample: A release reaches production without log routing or rollback authority.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Deployment is a controlled operational handoff.

nodes.label: Operations Maintenance
nodes.definition: Sustained configuration, identity, vulnerability, monitoring, backup, incident, and change control.
nodes.detail: Sustained configuration, identity, vulnerability, monitoring, backup, incident, and change control.
nodes.decision: Use evidence and review to keep protection effective as the system and threats change.
nodes.failureExample: A secure launch drifts into broad access after months of unreviewed changes.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Security must be operated, not merely delivered.
